e: API Gateway sends raw device data to a Kinesis data stream, and Firehose delivers it to S3: a managed, highly scalable ingestion path for millions of devices. Glue processes the raw data serverlessly. Adding EC2 instances or Route 53 routing keeps servers to manage.

With versioning enabled, the lifecycle rule deleted only current versions, which become noncurrent versions that remain and keep the object count rising. Adding rules to expire noncurrent (previous) versions deletes them after 3 years at no extra cost. A Lambda function would add cost and work.

Writing to an SQS queue first buffers bursts so no data is lost, and Lambda consumes from the queue at a controlled concurrency, reducing the number of database connections. A bigger instance or Multi-AZ doesn't handle bursts or connection counts, and SNS doesn't buffer messages for retries.

Aurora Serverless for MySQL automatically scales compute capacity up and down with demand, is MySQL-compatible, and offers better performance and durability with minimal operations. PostgreSQL isn't compatible with MySQL, and larger EC2 instances or an Auto Scaling group don't simplify database scaling.

NAT gateways are managed, scale automatically, and are highly available within an AZ; using one in each AZ gives fault tolerance. Two in the same AZ doesn't protect against an AZ failure, and NAT instances with Auto Scaling or Spot are complex and not automatically scalable.

VPC peering gives private connectivity between the VPCs over the AWS network, without exposing the database to the internet. Using public IP addresses, making the database public, or proxying through an Elastic IP instance is less secure.

VPC Flow Logs published to CloudWatch Logs can be filtered for traffic on ports 22 (SSH) and 3389 (RDP), and a metric filter with a CloudWatch alarm notifies the team when connections occur. Instance state-change events, Application Insights, or SSM roles don't detect SSH/RDP sessions.

Secure the root user with a strong password and multi-factor authentication. Don't create or store root access keys, and don't use the root user for routine permissions; the root user can't be added to groups or limited with IAM policies.

Use KMS keys to encrypt EBS volumes and Aurora storage at rest, and attach an ACM certificate to the ALB (HTTPS) to encrypt data in transit. ACM manages TLS certificates, not volume encryption, and KMS doesn't issue ALB certificates.

Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration, so use the Schema Conversion Tool for schema conversion and DMS with a full load plus CDC task to keep the databases in sync during the phased migration. A memory-optimized replication instance suits the heavy read/write change processing. DataSync isn't for databases.

Elastic Beanstalk Multi-AZ environments make the front end and application tiers scalable and available with little change to the application, RDS Multi-AZ provides a managed highly available MySQL database, and S3 stores and serves images. DynamoDB would require rewriting the database layer.

VPC peering works across accounts, is private, and has no single point of failure or bandwidth bottleneck because it uses the AWS backbone. Gateway endpoints don't support EC2, and a virtual private gateway or private VIF are for on-premises connections.

AWS Budgets lets you create a monthly cost budget per account scoped to EC2, with an alert threshold notifying an SNS topic as soon as it's exceeded. It's low cost, while Cost Explorer reports can't send threshold alerts, and CUR with Athena is much more setup.

A Lambda function URL provides a built-in HTTPS endpoint and supports AWS_IAM authentication, with no API Gateway or other components to set up, which is the most operationally efficient. Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions add needless complexity, and API Gateway is more than needed.

Hosting the visualization tool in the same Region as the data warehouse keeps the large 50 MB query results inside AWS (no egress), and only the small 500 KB pages go to users over Direct Connect, which has lower data transfer rates than the internet. Querying the warehouse from on premises sends the bigger payloads out.

An RDS for PostgreSQL instance with a cross-Region read replica keeps data available and online in another Region with a managed feature and little operational effort. Multi-AZ is within one Region, snapshot copies aren't online, and a self-managed cluster on EC2 is high overhead.

A multivalue answer routing policy returns up to eight healthy records in response to DNS queries and uses health checks, so unhealthy instances are excluded. Simple routing doesn't use health checks, and latency or geolocation policies return one answer.

An S3 File Gateway deployed as a VM at each clinic exposes the S3 data over NFS/SMB to on-premises file-based applications and caches frequently accessed files locally for low latency. Volume gateway gives block storage, DataSync copies data, and EFS can't be directly mounted by on-premises servers without special connectivity.

Moving the database to Aurora with a replica in another AZ, and using an AMI with an Auto Scaling group and ALB across two AZs, makes both tiers highly available and scalable. Options that keep instances in a single AZ or manual launches don't provide HA or scaling.

The development environment doesn't need the production capacity; running just one instance as a target cuts cost the most. Changing the balancing algorithm doesn't save money, and reducing the production instance size would hurt production.

An internet-facing ALB must be in public subnets (subnets with a route to an internet gateway) in each AZ the targets use. Create public subnets in each AZ and associate them with the ALB; the targets can stay in private subnets. (The route should lead to the internet gateway for the public subnets; the answer's description is simplified.)

Before creating a read replica for RDS MySQL, automated backups must be enabled (backup retention period not 0), and long-running transactions on the source should complete so the replica creation is not delayed or inconsistent. Global tables are a DynamoDB feature, and failover priority isn't a requirement.

Putting requests in an SQS queue and scaling an EC2 Auto Scaling group on queue size means no job is lost and capacity matches the load. A single bigger instance or a copy behind an ALB doesn't scale with demand, and an S3 endpoint doesn't affect CPU.

Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed service that provides SMB file shares. Volume gateway and tape gateway don't offer SMB file shares (file gateway does), and a Windows file share on EC2 is self-managed.

VPC Flow Logs can be delivered to S3, and a lifecycle policy moves them to Standard-IA after 90 days when access becomes intermittent, which is cost-effective. CloudTrail isn't a flow log target, and CloudWatch Logs with expiration or Kinesis would delete or not store the logs long term.
